items.claim: AGENTS.md declares `packages/core` must import no Node and no DOM. Node is in fact mechanically blocked (core/tsconfig.json sets `"types": []`, and pnpm's strict workspace linking means `@ledrums/io` would not resolve from core at all), but DOM is not: core inherits `"lib": ["ES2022", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"]` from tsconfig.base.json, so `document`, `window`, `fetch`, `localStorage` and friends would typecheck silently inside the pure package. The hole is not hypothetical — `voice/engine.ts:814` already reaches for the ambient `performance` global, whose type comes only from lib.dom.d.ts. It is the single reference standing between core and a DOM-free lib setting.

evidence.detail: packages/core/tsconfig.json extends ../../tsconfig.base.json and overrides only outDir/rootDir/types/moduleResolution — it does not narrow `lib`. tsconfig.base.json line 7: "lib": ["ES2022", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"].
Every hit is inside a comment (the word "window" in freeze.ts/strobe.ts, "document" in canvas/*.ts prose). No DOM API is actually called.
Exactly one real usage: packages/core/src/voice/engine.ts:814 `return typeof performance !== 'undefined' && typeof performance.now === 'function' ? performance.now() : 0;`
Core's only non-relative imports are 'vitest' (69, test files) and 'zod' (2). Zero node: imports, zero @ledrums/io imports — the Node half of the rule holds today.

items.proposed_fix: Add `"lib": ["ES2022"]` to packages/core/tsconfig.json's compilerOptions, and rewrite perfNow to reach the host clock through globalThis (an ES2020 lib symbol) instead of the DOM ambient: `const p = (globalThis as { performance?: { now?: () => number } }).performance; return typeof p?.now === 'function' ? p.now() : 0;`. The feature-detect fallback is preserved verbatim; only the type source changes. `pnpm --filter @ledrums/core typecheck` then becomes a real purity gate.

removes_failure_path.justification: The proposed rewrite keeps the exact `typeof … !== 'undefined'` / `typeof …now === 'function'` feature-detect and the `: 0` fallback; it only changes where the type for `performance` comes from.

steps: Run `pnpm --filter @ledrums/core typecheck` — it should fail on voice/engine.ts:814 only, proving that is the sole DOM dependency
Apply the globalThis rewrite and re-run typecheck; it must pass
Run `pnpm --filter @ledrums/core test` to confirm perf stats still populate

items.claim: AGENTS.md states three import-boundary rules as non-negotiable (core imports no Node/DOM/IO; all IO lives behind packages/io interfaces; core never imports io). CI runs only `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test`. There is no ESLint config anywhere in the repo, no `no-restricted-imports`, no dependency-cruiser, and no madge/cycle gate — madge, knip and depcheck exist as devDependencies but are invoked only ad hoc, not from any script in CI. The rules therefore hold today purely by author discipline, and as finding 1 shows the typecheck does not in fact cover the DOM half of the rule.

evidence.detail: .github/workflows/ci.yml: the `checks` job steps are checkout, pnpm setup, node setup, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`. The `desktop` job builds the sidecar and cargo. No lint or boundary step in either.
No .eslintrc*, eslint.config.*, or .dependency-cruiser.* at the repo root. knip.json exists but only lists entry points for unused-export detection, not boundary rules.
docs/plans/2026-07-26-deep-review/00-raw/depcheck.json shows madge/knip/depcheck as root devDependencies — tooling present, but nothing in package.json scripts or ci.yml runs them.

items.proposed_fix: Add a `boundaries` step to the CI `checks` job that fails on violation. Minimal version needs no new dependency: a vitest test in packages/core that globs src/**/*.ts and asserts no import specifier matches /^node:|^@ledrums\/(io|protocol)$/, plus finding 1's `lib: ["ES2022"]` to cover DOM. Fuller version: add a dependency-cruiser config with three forbidden rules (core→node builtins, core→@ledrums/io, core→@ledrums/protocol) and run `depcruise` in CI.

removes_failure_path.justification: This adds a fail-closed gate; it removes no guard, branch, retry or fallback.

items.claim: madge cycles #1 and #2 (reported four times over, once per unit that compiles core) both exist only because the pure data interface `Mapping` lives in `voice/modulation.ts`, a module that also holds runtime code and pulls in envelope → easing → types. `voice/types.ts:7` imports `ResolvedModifier` from `../modifiers/types`, and `modifiers/types.ts:23` imports `Mapping` back out of `../voice/modulation`, closing the loop. The cycle is type-only in both back-edges so it is harmless at runtime (see coverage notes), but it makes the generic modifier layer look like it depends on the voice engine, and it is the single largest contributor to the repo's reported cycle count.

evidence.detail: modifiers/types.ts:23 `import type { Mapping } from '../voice/modulation';`  voice/types.ts:7 `import type { ResolvedModifier } from '../modifiers/types';`  voice/types.ts:11 `import type { Mapping } from './modulation';`  voice/modulation.ts:17-20 imports sampleEnvelope (runtime) from ./envelope, sampleLfo from ./lfo, types from ./types.
Line 175 — `Mapping` is a plain interface with no runtime counterpart, sitting in the runtime module rather than in voice/types.ts where every other shared voice type lives.
Cycles 1 and 2 of packages/core, repeated as cycles 1-2 of protocol, server and web (8 of the 24 reported cycles trace to this one declaration site).

items.proposed_fix: Move `interface Mapping` (and any purely-type companions it needs) from voice/modulation.ts into voice/types.ts, then have voice/modulation.ts `export type { Mapping } from './types';` so every existing import path keeps working. modifiers/types.ts:23 can then import it from '../voice/types', a leaf type module, and madge cycles #1 and #2 disappear with zero runtime change.

removes_failure_path.justification: Moving a type declaration between modules removes no guard, validation or error branch.

steps: Move the Mapping interface into voice/types.ts and re-export from voice/modulation.ts
Run `pnpm typecheck` across the workspace — no consumer import should need changing
Run `npx madge --circular --extensions ts packages/core/src` and confirm cycles 1 and 2 are gone

items.claim: madge cycles #3, #4 and #5 all have the same shape: a big runtime module (render-plan.ts, engine.ts) calls into a helper, and the helper imports its own result/argument types straight back out of the caller. render-plan.ts:2-3 runtime-imports detectEmptyScopes and detectUnreachable; both lint files then type-import RenderPlanChild/RenderPlanIssue from './render-plan'. diagnostics.ts:1 type-imports InputEvent from './engine', which engine.ts:59 runtime-imports back. All four back-edges are `import type` so nothing is load-order fragile, but the type declarations are living in the wrong modules: RenderPlanIssue/RenderPlanChild and InputEvent are contract types, not implementation details of the modules that happen to produce them.

packages/core cycles 3) voice/engine.ts > voice/diagnostics.ts, 4) voice/render-plan.ts > voice/reachability-lint.ts, 5) voice/render-plan.ts > voice/scope-lint.ts — repeated per consuming unit (12 of the 24 reported cycles).

items.claim: tsconfig.base.json sets `verbatimModuleSyntax: true`, which means TypeScript emits an `import { voice } from '@ledrums/core'` statement verbatim even when every use of `voice` is a type position. In these four modules `voice` appears exclusively in type positions (voice.RenderPlanIssue, voice.EnvKind, voice.Mapping, …), so each file creates an unnecessary runtime dependency on core's barrel — which is not side-effect free (packages/core/src/index.ts:34 re-exports canvas/presets, whose module body registers every builtin scene). These should be `import type { voice }`.

evidence.detail: Line 12 `import { voice } from '@ledrums/core';` then lines 15, 27, 37, 52, 61, 75, 77 use only voice.RenderPlanIssue / voice.RenderPlanIssueCode — all type positions. Same pattern in lint-preview.svelte.ts (lines 17, 19), GraphLintStrip.svelte (line 15), sim.envelopes.ts (lines 16-28, a block of `export type X = voice.X` aliases).

items.claim: The module header states "Type-only import — adds NO runtime dependency on core (core stays pure)." Line 18 is `import { voice } from '@ledrums/core';` — a value import — and lines 57-60 call `voice.isModSourceKind(kind)` at runtime. The comment is the load-bearing record of an import-boundary decision and it is false, which is exactly the kind of note a future reader would trust instead of re-checking. (The dependency itself is legitimate: apps/web is allowed to depend on core. Only the claim is wrong.)

evidence.detail: apps/web/src/lib/trigger-lab/sim.graph-compilation.ts lines 13-14: "Type-only import — adds NO runtime dependency on core (core stays pure)." Line 18: `import { voice } from '@ledrums/core';`
Line 57: `export const nodeHasOutput = (kind: NodeKind): boolean => kind !== 'output' && !voice.isModSourceKind(kind);` and line 60 likewise — runtime calls into the core barrel.

items.proposed_fix: Rewrite the NOTE to state the truth: the graph TYPES are aliased from core, and the module additionally takes a runtime dependency on core for `voice.isModSourceKind`. Do not silence it by switching to `import type` — that would break the two runtime call sites.
